policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere תֵּת and ketiv תתן are the same lemma (5414) parsed the same way (Vqc), differing only in orthography. "until the day that Jehovah sendeth rain upon the earth" renders either identically, and the ASV carries no note here. Base fallback retained.

The readings differ in gender order: qere הִיא וָהוּא is feminine then masculine, ketiv הוא והיא the reverse. The ASV's "and she, and he, and her house, did eat" puts the widow first, which is the qere.
